incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (water, energy, manufacturing, chemical, food)
incidents.vector: Attackers scan for internet-exposed Siemens S7 series PLCs and use AI-generated exploitation scripts (built on the open-source snap7 library) disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to gain read/write access via the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warned of an 'active threat' involving persistent reconnaissance and pre-positioning against S7 PLCs, which could enable disruption of industrial processes, safety incidents or equipment damage; the advisory is unattributed but follows recent Iran-linked targeting of water utilities.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an internet-exposed CSDD system after targeted preparation; several mandatory cybersecurity requirements had reportedly not been met.
incidents.impact: Data from payment receipts dating to 2008 was stolen, exposing personal ID numbers, license plates and addresses for more than 1.2 million people and 200,000 businesses (roughly two-thirds of Latvia's population); the president called it a national security threat and the agency's supervisory board resigned.

incidents.victim: Healthcare and critical infrastructure organizations (500+ victims)
incidents.vector: Medusa affiliates buy access from initial access brokers and exploit unpatched software, weaponizing newly announced exploits within 24 hours and sometimes up to a week before public disclosure, then use living-off-the-land and legitimate RMM tools.
incidents.impact: An updated CISA/FBI/HHS advisory reported Medusa has hit more than 500 victims as of April 2026 (up from 300), with heavy focus on healthcare; the group uses double and even triple extortion.

incidents.victim: US and foreign universities, companies and government agencies
incidents.vector: The Iran-based Mabna Institute ran spearphishing campaigns against professor accounts using stolen credentials to access university systems and email inboxes.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 members of the Mabna Institute for a campaign that compromised ~8,000 professor accounts across 144 US and 178 foreign universities and stole at least 31.5 terabytes of academic data and IP on behalf of the IRGC; a $10M reward was offered for five defendants.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: Threat activity was detected at the edge of the university's academic network over the weekend and contained before reaching core systems.
incidents.impact: The university, serving 40,000 students, took systems including phones offline days before classes began, extended payment deadlines and forced a campus-wide password reset; no evidence of data exfiltration was reported and no group claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: Two Berlin state ministries (urban development; transport/environment)
incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly exploited a vulnerability in the IT systems of one affected ministry, according to government sources cited by public broadcaster RBB.
incidents.impact: Berlin isolated two ministries from the city government network as a precaution after discovering a security breach; employees lost email and internet access and some public services such as housing benefit applications were disrupted.

incidents.vector: A ransomware affiliate emails victims mid-incident (before attacks are public) posing as an incident-recovery service called 'Ransom Busters,' claiming to have infiltrated RaaS operators' infrastructure and offering to delete stolen data for a $20,000-$60,000 Bitcoin fee.
incidents.impact: GuidePoint assessed with moderate confidence that Ransom Busters is a single affiliate working across DragonForce, Settra and Anubis operations, using its access to divert ransom payments away from the original ransomware groups; victims have no assurance data is actually deleted.

incidents.vector: The Python-based 'TwinLoot' framework runs its entire command-and-control from inside Microsoft Azure and 365 services (SharePoint, Graph API, Teams TURN relay, the victim's own Edge browser), harvests credentials via fake lock screens and achieves persistence via an offline-forged mandatory profile hive.
incidents.impact: Ontinue researchers discovered the modular implant during a July campaign; it provides a reverse SOCKS5 pivot for lateral movement while disguising all activity as legitimate cloud traffic, defeating domain-reputation and IP-blocking controls.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity and law firms
incidents.vector: BlackFile (tracked as UNC6671) impersonates IT helpdesk staff in voice-phishing calls to employees' personal phones, luring them to adversary-in-the-middle passkey/SSO portals that harvest credentials and MFA tokens, then exfiltrates data from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Google/Mandiant and CyberScoop report the group, linked to The Com, remains active after rebranding across Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon leak sites, targeting ~1.5 new big-game victims daily; extortion demands often start around $3M and some victims have faced swatting.

incidents.vector: An actor using the handle 'TheHatman' claims to have used compromised credentials via MFA-fatigue and password-spraying attacks to exfiltrate data from organizations' Microsoft Entra tenants.
incidents.impact: From Aug 1-17 the actor advertised employee and enterprise data for sale across multiple forums, with public reporting naming claimed victims including McDonald's, Vodafone and Kyndryl; Unit 42 has not verified a specific intrusion vector or the claims.

incidents.vector: The 'JWR' phishing-as-a-service framework impersonates checkout and login pages for payment platforms (Shopify, PayPal, Apple, Klarna, banks), delivered via SMS lures impersonating toll and postal authorities, with an operator steering victim sessions live over an encrypted WebSocket.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos detailed the real-time framework — a likely variant of 'The Outsider' PhaaS run by a Chinese-speaking actor — which harvests card data, credentials, 2FA codes, SSNs and identity documents while bypassing MFA in real time; campaigns were observed across Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

incidents.vector: A Chinese-language operator used a multi-agent AI framework built on OpenClaw and Hermes, running up to eight coordinated subagents to autonomously conduct reconnaissance, crack credentials, exploit vulnerabilities, exfiltrate records and install backdoors.
incidents.impact: Sovereign AI firm Dream documented what it called the first 'near-autonomous' AI attack on a nation-state, spanning 12 attack waves over four days; Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs acknowledged AI-driven attacks on government agencies matching the description.

incidents.victim: Android TV boxes and IoT devices
incidents.vector: Kimwolf v7 spreads via residential proxies to reach unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge instances on port 5555, and adds an HTTP/2 flood with browser-fingerprint spoofing plus resilient three-tier C2 using Ethereum Name Service, a Tor hidden service and a local proxy.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 identified the upgraded Kimwolf/AISURU botnet variant, hardened to survive prior takedowns (including a March 2026 DOJ-led seizure), which powers high-performance DDoS attacks from infected set-top boxes; C2 hosts cluster in Saint Petersburg, Russia.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack struck the ministry a day after Colombia's national CERT warned that ransomware groups had increased their focus on the country.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted some services around illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes days before the country's presidential transition.

incidents.victim: Government, healthcare, financial and critical infrastructure organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Gunra affiliates deploy ransomware using a double-extortion model, encrypting data while exfiltrating business-critical documents, databases and PII, and use stealth techniques such as deleting access logs and clearing command history.
incidents.impact: NSA, FBI and partners released a #StopRansomware advisory on the Gunra RaaS, which emerged in 2025 and expanded to affiliate operations in 2026, hitting victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached systems at the shipping giant and stole customer order data.
incidents.impact: A data breach at Ceva Logistics affected at least eight warehouses across Europe and rippled to banks, retailers and Steam gamers, with stolen data including customer names, home addresses, phone numbers and email addresses.

incidents.vector: The Aeternum C++ botnet loader shifts its entire command-and-control onto the public Polygon blockchain via smart contracts, uses VM detection and antivirus evasion, and downloads secondary payloads (including XWorm RAT and XMRig miner) from GitHub with Telegram API exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 analyzed the resilient, low-cost loader that establishes persistence and exfiltrates data; its decentralized blockchain C2 complicates law-enforcement takedown efforts.

incidents.vector: The self-propagating 'ChainDrop' npm worm (linked to the Shai-Hulud/keyv compromise) infects packages via a preinstall hook that runs an obfuscated payload, harvesting cloud credentials, npm/GitHub tokens, SSH keys and CI runner memory secrets, then republishes additional packages using stolen tokens.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found ChainDrop infected over 400 packages downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly (including keyv and cacheable-request), exposing developer workstations, CI pipelines and cloud environments; attackers reconfigured C2 via a single Ethereum transaction.

incidents.vector: Between February and October 2024, Connor Moucka ('Judische'/'Waifu') and co-conspirators used stolen credentials to access cloud-hosted data of at least 165 customers of a SaaS provider (Snowflake) that lacked MFA, then extorted victims by threatening to publish the data.
incidents.impact: The Canadian man pleaded guilty to computer fraud, wire fraud and aggravated identity theft; the conspiracy stole billions of records (including AT&T call/text logs for 100M+ customers), netted over $2.5M in ransoms and caused victims over $9.5M in losses. He faces up to 30 years.
